active_forecast_assumption.basis: run_forecast_model inferred a 0.977% monthly growth rate from the 7-month trailing revenue series Feb-Aug 2026 ($1.415M -> $1.500M). MoM growth decelerated from 1.06% (Feb->Mar) down to ~0.885-0.90% (Apr-Jul) before rebounding to 1.215% in Jul->Aug. Using the smoothed 7-month inferred rate rather than chasing the single latest uptick avoids overstating the forecast off one month.

fpa_report.summary: August 2026: Revenue grew to $1.50M (+1.2% MoM, consistent with the ~1% trailing trend), but gross margin fell to 73.05% from 78% in Jun (76% in Jul) — a real, sustained slide driven entirely by rising hosting/infrastructure COGS, not revenue mix or pricing. Opex budget variances were mostly within normal range (<5%) except a $18.2K/28% overspend in Marketing and a full $6.9K miss on Sales commissions. Revenue forecast assumption reaffirmed at ~0.98% monthly growth, closely matching the already-active 0.99% assumption, so it was set directly without requiring approval.
material_variances: COGS - Hosting & Infrastructure (not a budgeted line, but the real margin driver): grew from $315,180 (21.5% of revenue) in Jun to $347,680 (23.5%) in Jul to $396,200 (26.4%) in Aug, while Third-Party Data Costs held flat at $8,000/mo and revenue grew only ~1%/mo over the same period. This 3-month divergence between infrastructure cost growth (+10.3% Jun->Jul, +14.0% Jul->Aug) and revenue growth is the sole driver of the gross margin decline from 78% to 73.05%.

MKT / marketing account: actual $83,037 vs budget $64,873, +28% ($18,164 over). Also a sharp sequential jump from $43,531 (Jul) and $45,815 (Jun) to $83,037 (Aug) -- roughly double the prior two months' run-rate, consistent with a one-time or lumpy campaign spend rather than a new sustained baseline.

SALES / commissions: actual $0 vs budget $6,904, a -100% variance. Dollar impact is small but the complete miss (not just underperformance) alongside Sales salaries being fully paid and slightly over budget (+3.45%) is anomalous and warrants confirmation of whether this is a timing/accrual gap or a genuine absence of commissionable bookings in August.

All other opex lines (G&A facilities +4.94%, G&A salaries -3.72%, Sales salaries +3.45%, G&A software -2.98%, Marketing salaries -2.73%, Professional fees -2.64%, Customer Success salaries +2.37%, Engineering salaries -2.16%) were within +/-5% of budget and consistent with normal payroll/operating fluctuation -- not flagged as material.
findings: Gross margin fell from 78% (Feb-Jun 2026, flat) to 76% (Jul) to 73.05% (Aug) -- a genuine 3-month downtrend, not a one-off blip.

The margin decline traces entirely to COGS: Hosting & Infrastructure cost as a % of revenue rose from 21.5% (Jun) to 26.4% (Aug), while Third-Party Data Costs stayed flat at $8,000/mo and revenue grew steadily (~1%/mo). No budget line exists for hosting COGS in the system, so this trend did not surface in the standard budget-variance scan and required direct income-statement comparison across months to catch.

Budget variance scan (2026-08, all departments) surfaced 10 lines; by dollar and % combined, the two material ones were Marketing (+28%/$18.2K, a clear step-up vs. the $43-46K run-rate of the prior two months) and Sales commissions (-100%/$6.9K, a complete miss worth confirming with Sales/AR for timing vs. real cause).

Revenue history Feb-Aug 2026 shows steady MoM growth decelerating from 1.06% to ~0.885-0.90% (Mar-Jul) before rebounding to 1.215% in the latest month (Jul->Aug). run_forecast_model inferred a smoothed 0.977% monthly rate from this 7-month window.

Set the 2026-09 forecast assumption at 0.98% monthly growth, based on the 7-month trailing revenue trend. This is within 1pp of the already-active 0.99% assumption (inferred from an overlapping 8-month Jan-Aug window), so the system accepted it directly -- no human approval required.

Deliberately did not fold the hosting-cost or marketing-spend trends into the revenue growth rate itself, since neither is a revenue data point; they are flagged in the assumption notes as risk factors (potential margin/unit-economics deterioration, and a sales-commission anomaly worth investigating) for the CFO to weigh before the next forecast cycle.

cfo_briefing.summary: Meridian Analytics posted an operating loss of -$528,400 in 2026-08 on revenue of $1.50M, with gross margin compressing to 73.05% and payroll at 98.73% of revenue. Cash burned -$661,519 in the month, leaving $2,167,718 ending cash and only 4.4 months of runway at the trailing average burn rate. Payroll itself is confirmed on-budget by the payroll specialist; the controller confirms books are clean (no integrity issue behind the $0 balance-sheet liabilities). The real driver of deterioration, per FP&A, is accelerating hosting/infrastructure COGS eroding gross margin, compounded by a one-off marketing overspend in August, with no cost-reduction plan currently offsetting the trend.

hypotheses: The primary driver of margin compression is rising hosting/infrastructure unit costs outpacing revenue growth (COGS +27% vs revenue +3% over Feb-Aug) — this looks like an infrastructure scaling/efficiency problem rather than a one-off, and warrants vendor/usage review.

August's marketing overspend (+28% vs budget) appears to be a one-time or discretionary spend rather than a structural shift, since prior months (Jun/Jul) did not show this pattern — but this is unconfirmed and should be validated with whoever approved the marketing spend.
Payroll growth is currently well-managed and not the primary risk to runway; the CS and Sales overtime/budget overages are modest and likely workload-driven rather than a control issue.

At current trend (no intervention), the company is on a trajectory toward faster cash depletion than the current 4.4-month runway estimate implies, since burn has been accelerating (not flat) for three consecutive months.
recommendations: Prioritize a hosting/infrastructure cost review (vendor contracts, usage efficiency, architecture) given COGS growth is outpacing revenue by a wide margin and is the largest identified lever on gross margin.
Have FP&A and the budget owner review and confirm whether the August marketing overspend (+$18.2K vs budget) was approved/one-off or is likely to recur in September.

Given 4.4 months of runway and an accelerating (not stabilizing) burn trend with no cost-reduction plan on file, management/board should discuss near-term financing options and/or a formal burn-reduction plan before runway compresses further.
Ask FP&A to build an explicit cost-reduction scenario (not just revenue-growth extrapolation) into the forecast model so runway projections reflect planned mitigations, not just trailing trend.
No action needed on the $0 balance-sheet liabilities — controller confirmed this is expected under pay-as-incurred AP handling, not an error.
open_questions: What specifically drove the 27% rise in hosting/infrastructure costs since May (usage growth, price increases, new services, inefficiency)? No specialist was asked to break this down at the vendor/usage level — would need AP or a dedicated infra cost review.
Was the August marketing overspend a planned one-time campaign or an emerging trend? FP&A flagged it as new but did not confirm the underlying cause or leadership's intent for September.
Is there a company-approved plan (financing, cost cuts, revenue acceleration) to address the sub-5-month runway, or is management currently unaware of the accelerating burn trend FP&A identified?

The company uses pay-as-incurred AP with no liability accrual — is this the intended accounting policy going forward, or should period-end AP accruals be introduced for more accurate point-in-time liability reporting? (Controller flagged it as not an error, but did not weigh in on policy preference.)
